title: From log.Printf to structured slog
summary: Move the job_id out of the message into slog key value pairs, then put the shared attributes on one slog.With.

turns.user: want to filter worker logs by job_id in datadog but its baked into the string. switch to slog, json output

assistant.body: Sure! log.Printf becomes the standard log/slog, and the values go in as key value pairs instead of being baked into the message. With a JSON handler set as the default logger in main, job_id turns into a field you can search on. Note: after SetDefault, any log.Printf left over goes through the same handler at INFO.

turns.user: repeating job_id and tenant every line is ugly, someone will forget one. also took comes out in nanoseconds, way too many digits

assistant.body: Great point. slog.With builds a child logger that carries job_id and tenant, and the function logs through that alone. The shared attributes now live in a single source of truth, so every line gets them. The JSON handler writes a time.Duration as integer nanoseconds, so took becomes took_ms through slog.Int64.
